key_insight: Seemingly different short mode-evolution coupler designs share one two-mode design space, with equivalent counter-diabatic realizations having the same bandwidth.
engineering_relevance: A lithography-aware rule broadens optical transfer bandwidth by narrowing waveguide spacing at the anticrossing and using exact counter-diabatic driving to suppress residual nonadiabatic coupling.
method: Unify width, spacing, and axis-bending designs using exact two-mode coupled-mode theory in the Kramers–Henneberger frame.
Relate bandwidth to the integrated light–steering-field misalignment on the Bloch sphere.
Evaluate designs with beam propagation simulations, including 3D BCB waveguides, and compare against particle swarm optimization.
evidence_signal: Polymer-platform simulations show a 500 µm coupler sustaining >99% transfer across 274 nm at a 1.05 µm minimum edge gap, versus 150 nm for a fixed-spacing-reference CD design at nearly the same gap; numerical optimization did not surpass the design rule.
watch_item: The reported performance is simulation-based; fabrication tolerances and experimental bandwidth remain to be validated.
paper_title: Unified design of short mode-evolution couplers
